hard_case: `#[macro_use] mod support;` makes a table generator defined in `tests/support/mod.rs` visible to the file that invokes it; the middle row sits on the limit.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 5 against a limit of 5 no longer fits
not equivalent: 6 against a limit of 5 now fits

reasoning: Rows import_under(3, 5, true), import_at(5, 5, true) and import_over(6, 5, false) sit under and on both sides of the limit, so `limit > width` fails import_at and `limit + 1 >= width` fails import_over. The generator `imported_table!` is defined in tests/support/mod.rs; tests/modules.rs imports it with `#[macro_use] mod support;` and invokes it, so ripr has to resolve the definition from another file.
